data.narrative:
Colossal Biosciences, a Series C-stage biotech company founded by Ben Lamm and George Church, is evaluated against a comp universe of 3 public equities (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, with particular relevance to Chai Discovery ($3.8B), New Limit ($3.1B), and Eikon Therapeutics ($539M). The company has raised $555M+ to reach a current post-money valuation of $10.32B.

Two triangulation methods were applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x typical step-up multiplier from Series C to next stage, yielding $17.5B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies produces a $3.1B implied value, with a range spanning $539M to $3.8B. Public-comp anchoring could not be applied—while the Biotech & Health sector trades at a 5.5x median price-to-sales across the three public comps, Colossal's revenue is not on file, precluding this method.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $2.6B (low) to $20.2B (high), with a median of $10.3B anchored to the current post-money valuation. The wide dispersion reflects tension between stage-progression momentum and peer comparables trading significantly below current valuation. Key uncertainties include revenue scale (unavailable for public-comp calibration), the relevance of stage-progression multipliers in frontier biotech, and comparability of the peer set across development and commercialization maturity.
